observation.description: The client's default persistence ladder (rqs-store-default.mjs: explicit option, env off, browser IndexedDB+WebLocks, node filesystem, in-memory) has no React Native arm, so on the Expo carrier every client silently resolves the in-memory store (rqsStoreInfo {implementation:'memory', durable:false}). LLP 0129 Phase 0's 'the client cache persists across cold boots BY DEFAULT' therefore does not extend to the documented mobile carrier: no cold-boot retained render, and even after f2 is fixed the queue would not survive process death. The receipt's cold-restart leg (EXPO-06) evidences the honest outcome: the app relaunches offline into a 'backend unreachable' state with zero rows, freshness/retention machinery never engaging.

competitorOutcome.description: Firestore RN ships on-device offline persistence so a cold offline relaunch renders prior data; InstantDB's RN client persists its cache similarly (frozen A1 bar: cached rows plus queued writes after relaunch).

mustNotRegress: The refuse-with-clarity honesty: retention must stay opt-in, authority-scoped, reported via rqsStoreInfo/retention facts, with zero protected bytes at rest outside lease custody - never Firebase-style silent protected-row caching.
smallestCoherentFix: An RN store arm in the resolution ladder (expo-file-system or SQLite-backed implementation of the persisted-entry contract rqs-store-file.mjs already defines), selected on RN with the same DK-9 capability reporting, plus a react-expo guide section on mobile retention.
acceptanceWitness: On an Expo simulator, a retainable public query cold-boots offline with freshness 'retained' / connection 'stale' from the on-device store, and the sentinel grep proves no protected bytes at rest - the web arm's A1-05/06 facts reproduced on the mobile carrier.
